events.title: Joomla 2.5 released
events.summary: The [Joomla] project shipped [Joomla] 2.5 on January 24, 2012 — the first long-term support release in the 2.x series.
events.about: [Joomla] 2.5 added one-click core updates, multi-language support in core, and a refined ACL system — bridging [Joomla] 1.5 sites toward the Bootstrap-based [Joomla] 3 admin. It was the stable branch most production [Joomla] sites ran through the early 2010s.

narrative.whyChosen: [Joomla] 2.5 was the [LTS] release that carried the [Joomla] ecosystem through the 2.x era.
narrative.whyImportant: Core multilingual support and one-click updates reduced upgrade friction for thousands of sites.
narrative.problemSolved: [Joomla] 1.5 sites needed a supported path forward with modern security and localization.

events.title: SOPA/PIPA protest blackout mobilizes the web
events.summary: On January 18, 2012, Wikipedia, Reddit, Google, and thousands of sites blacked out or protested the Stop Online Piracy Act and PROTECT [IP] Act — congressional bills that would have expanded copyright enforcement online.
events.about: The coordinated protest generated millions of emails to Congress and shelved both bills within days. It showed developers and platform operators could wield political power as a bloc — a template later reused for net neutrality campaigns and EU copyright directive fights.

narrative.whyChosen: The blackout was the largest political protest in internet history.
narrative.whyImportant: It proved tech communities could kill legislation that threatened open platforms.
narrative.problemSolved: SOPA/PIPA would have forced sites to police user links and enabled domain seizures without full due process.
